genZNote: Without this hot-spring bacterium, PCR (and basically all of modern molecular diagnostics) wouldn't exist — its heat-stable polymerase is 'Taq' in every PCR kit.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Hot springs and other naturally occurring high-temperature aquatic environments
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: First isolated from Yellowstone hot springs; grows optimally around 70°C

microscopy.appearance: Gram-negative rods, often in filamentous chains

culture.growthCharacteristics: Grows optimally at 65-72°C, will not grow at standard 37°C incubation
culture.colonyMorphology: Yellow to orange-pigmented colonies from carotenoid pigments

identificationClues: True thermophile — requires incubation near 70°C and will not grow at typical clinical-lab temperatures (37°C)
Yellow-orange pigmented colonies from carotenoid pigments
Source of Taq DNA polymerase, the heat-stable enzyme that made automated PCR possible
Not a human pathogen — purely of biotechnological/historical importance

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Catalase and oxidase positive; grows only at high temperature
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Original natural source of Taq polymerase, the enzyme underlying modern PCR

sources.name: NCBI Bookshelf — overview of thermophilic bacteria and PCR history
